jobs.occupation: Analyst (Student Assistant), Technology and Solutions
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a global fund manager in energy infrastructure investments? If so, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) is currently looking for a Student Analyst to join our Technology & Solutions team based in Copenhagen.

Team

The Technology & Solutions team serves as CIP’s internal hub for emerging technologies, combining technical expertise with commercial and investment perspectives. The team assesses novel technologies and their maturity, tracks global technology developments and trends, and supports investment teams with technology screening, risk assessments and recommendations on new opportunities. The team also leads CIP’s energy system studies, such as the Charging Ahead report, CIP’s roadmap for an electrified, competitive and resilient European energy system towards 2050, and works with cross-functional teams to turn the findings into content supporting CIP’s global Investor Relations and Public Affairs efforts.

Role

As a Student Analyst, you will join a small, specialized team and work closely with CIP’s investment, Investor Relations and Public Affairs teams. This is a part-time position of on average 20 hours per week, with flexibility to accommodate both peak workloads and your studies, such as exam periods. The role offers broad exposure to emerging energy technologies, how they translate into investable projects, and how CIP communicates its view on the future energy system.

Responsibilities will consist of but are not limited to:

• Assist with technical and commercial assessments of novel technologies to support CIP’s internal knowledge hub

• Assist with novel technology screening of potential investment opportunities, assessing technology maturity, key technical and commercial risks and mitigation strategies, including impact on the business case

• Assist with mapping of global technology developments and trends to support CIP’s business development

• Analyse data for CIP’s energy system study (see Charging Ahead report), and work with cross-functional teams to develop content for Investor Relations and Public Affairs events

• Ad hoc assistance with reporting for function leadership

You

You are currently pursuing an Engineering BSc/MSc degree (e.g. DTU, such as energy-related engineering degrees, and Sustainable Energy Systems or Technologies), with at least 1.5-2 years of studies remaining. You have a keen interest in energy technologies and the energy transition, and ideally relevant experience from student jobs or internships involving assessment and communication of complex topics to senior colleagues. You have solid analytical skills, are detail oriented and can take responsibility and work independently on your tasks while being comfortable translating complex data into effective communication material.

We look for the following in a candidate:

• Good communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences

• Skilled at structuring and building clear, compelling slides and presentations

• Solid stakeholder management skills and comfortable collaborating with cross-functional teams

• Proactive and ambitious, with the motivation to take ownership of tasks and seek out new challenges

The process

Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

---

Building value that matters

Founded in 2012, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners P/S (CIP) today is the world’s largest dedicated fund manager within greenfield renewable energy investments and a global leader in offshore wind. To date, CIP has developed and constructed more than +50 greenfield renewable projects around the world. CIP is developing a greenfield project portfolio of ~160GW total, and ~16 GW is in operation or under construction. CIP manages 13 funds and has to date raised approximately EUR ~35 billion for investments in energy and associated infrastructure from more than ~200 international institutional investors.

CIP has a multinational team of ~500 full-time employees with extensive experience and knowledge within the fields of renewable energy project development and regulated infrastructure. In addition, CIP has a broad range of competencies within corporate finance, mergers & acquisitions, engineering, construction, project development, and project management.

CIP has built a prominent investment team capable of originating proprietary investment opportunities and executing projects and investments based on the team’s industrial background, large industrial network, and extensive experience in structuring, executing, and managing investments within energy infrastructure. Headquartered in Copenhagen, CIP also operates from key locations across the globe, including offices in Hamburg, Munich, London, Utrecht, New York, Tokyo, Melbourne, Luxembourg, Kuala Lumpur, Seoul and Singapore. In addition, CIP has 17 local project offices globally.

For more information, visit www.cip.com.

jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer – IoT Platform, Load and Energy Management
jobs.description:
🚀 About the role

We're looking for a senior software engineer who writes solid, reliable code and wants that code to control real hardware. At FLEXECHARGE, our HARMON-E platform manages load and energy for EV charging operators across Europe. Part of it runs at the edge, on an industrial PC next to chargers, batteries and solar inverters, and connected to the interfaces DSOs use to curtail load.

You'll build and maintain the TypeScript microservices that talk to those devices and turn their data into decisions. This is not a web-app role. It's software engineering for systems where the other side is physical, stateful and often unreliable.

⚡ What is special about this role

It sits where two worlds meet:

• 
Web and cloud toolchain: TypeScript, Docker, MQTT, Azure, Kubernetes.

• 
Operational technology and system integration: talking to real chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus and OCPP, running at the edge on an industrial PC.

Your code won't only talk to clean APIs in a data centre. It runs on site, next to real peripheral devices, and has to keep doing its job when those devices and the networks between them don't behave as expected.

We recognize that TypeScript is not typically used for edge computing or hardware interfacing. This is why we're looking for a strong software engineer who is interested in learning new techniques and applications, as well as applying their technical skills in novel ways.

🛠️ What you'll do

• 
Write and maintain a combination of TypeScript microservices and the business logic behind them: control algorithms, scheduling and decision-making, not just plumbing.

• 
Build and extend device drivers for chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus TCP, using our existing driver services as a starting point.

• 
Work with OCPP, which our platform already supports, as you ramp up.

• 
Run services in containers at the edge and connect them through MQTT and pub/sub messaging to our cloud backend.

• 
Profile and optimise software on edge hardware, where hardware resources are constrained.

• 
Help shape the long-term move of performance-critical services to compiled languages.

• 
Mentor and pair with colleagues on integrations and software craft.

🤔 Why compiled languages, if we write TypeScript?

It may sound odd, so here's the reasoning. Today the majority of our edge stack is TypeScript, and you'll develop in it from day one. Over time we want to move selected services, such as device interfaces and performance-critical paths, to a compiled language while keeping them part of the same stack.

To do that well, you need to understand both sides: the TypeScript services as they are now, and the concepts of memory, types and performance that compiled languages force you to think about. In our experience, it's much easier to go from a compiled language to a scripting environment than the other way around. So if you're a Go, C, C++, Rust or similar developer who is happy to work in TypeScript (or happy to learn), you're exactly who we're looking for.

✅ Must-have

• 
3–5+ years of professional software development, with strong software and engineering fundamentals.

• 
Professional experience in a compiled language (for example Go, C, C++, Rust, C# or Java).

• 
Proficiency in a scripting language, ideally TypeScript, otherwise JavaScript or Python, or a clear willingness to become productive in TypeScript quickly.

• 
Experience writing business logic with stateful calculations and operations, which can self-heal and recover gracefully.

• 
Comfort with asynchronous and event-driven systems that talk to unreliable external components or peripheral devices.

💡 Strongly preferred (but we'll teach it)

• 
Hands-on device or protocol integration: Modbus, serial interfaces, Ethernet/TCP-IP or comparable.

• 
Containerised applications. Docker, Docker Compose or Kubernetes are ideal, but any container technology counts.

• 
Pub/sub and distributed systems, ideally MQTT or another IoT messaging protocol, and an understanding of their reliability concerns.

• 
Working within constrained systems, including profiling software to find where CPU or memory limits bite.

🎁 Bonus, not a requirement

• 
OCPP experience.

• 
Energy, EV charging or power-systems domain knowledge.

• 
Edge deployment experience.

If you don't have these, apply anyway. Strong fundamentals and the right mindset matter more. 💪

🚫 This role is probably not for you if

• 
Your experience is mainly frontend or request/response web apps, with no compiled-language background.

• 
You prefer to stay in one language and aren't interested in working in TypeScript.

• 
You want a pure firmware or PLC role without writing higher-level services.

• 
You don't enjoy debugging the messy cases where hardware doesn't behave as documented.

🌆 What is it like to work at FLEXECHARGE?

• 
Our office is in Frederiksberg: bright, comfortable, and a genuinely nice place to spend your workday.

• 
You're covered with pension contributions.

• 
Lunch is served on-site, and it's delicious, healthy and nutritious.

• 
We enjoy each other's company outside work too, with Friday bars, company events and team-building activities within each team.

• 
You'll have opportunities for individual development.

🤝 Our interview process

Here's roughly what happens once we've had a look at your application:

• 
A first conversation (about 30 minutes) with our recruiter. You'll get a feel for the role, ask whatever's on your mind, and we'll both get a sense of whether this is worth pursuing further.

• 
Time with the team: a conversation with Kasper, our Head of Architecture & Systems, and Robert, our CTO.

• 
A technical stage: one or more interviews with the team, which may include a case exercise and follow-up discussions. These can take place remotely or at our office.

• 
A conversation with Max, our CEO, alongside someone else from the team.

Hiring carefully matters to us. We want to get to know you properly, and we want you to get a real feel for us too. If there's anything we can do to make the process work better for you, tell us.

We'd love to hear from you.

📍 Location & practical details

This is an on-site role based in Copenhagen. Only candidates currently located in Copenhagen, or those who clearly state in their application that they plan to relocate, will be considered.

Please note:

• 
We do not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

• 
We do not offer relocation services.

🔐 Data privacy (GDPR)

Applications for this role are processed exclusively through The Hub (thehub.io), our recruitment platform, in accordance with their privacy policy and applicable GDPR requirements. As part of our interview process, conversations may be recorded and transcribed via Microsoft Teams, and AI tools may be used to summarise interview notes to support our hiring team's evaluation. Your data will be handled confidentially, retained only during the interview process, and used only for this recruitment process.

For more information or questions please contact us at iva@flexecharge.com

Working at

FLEXECHARGE

FLEXECHARGE is a cleantech scale-up which offers a powerful load & energy management platform, as a SaaS, to help Charge Point Operators (ex: Clever, eOn, etc.) to optimise their charging operations & business. Our mission is accelerate green mobility through our Smart Charging solutions that make charging faster, greener and cheaper. Our vision is to integrate charging infrastructures better with the grid supply and the ever more volatile & growing production of renewable energy. We want to connect electric vehicles with the grid in a whole new way. By seeing electric vehicles not as a risk for our supply grid, but as a crucial asset for the transition towards 100% renewable energy. We do this through constant innovation of new smart charging features which will make us the preferred partner for EV infrastructure owners, developers, and operators.

jobs.occupation: PKPD Senior Principal Scientist
jobs.description:
Department: DMPK and Modelling Sciences

Location: [Måløv]

Your impact begins here

As a Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics (PKPD) Senior Principal Scientist, you will shape how translational modelling supports decisions across drug discovery and development. You will set direction for PKPD strategies, connect preclinical evidence with human safety and efficacy, and help interdisciplinary teams progress a diverse research portfolio. Your scientific leadership will strengthen project decisions from early research through clinical development and regulatory submission.

What you’ll bring

You bring deep expertise in translational science and mathematical modelling, together with the judgement to turn complex evidence into clear recommendations. You communicate effectively across disciplines, work independently and help colleagues solve scientific challenges.

• A PhD in pharmaceutical, medical, physical, mathematical or engineering sciences, or another relevant discipline, combined with substantial pharmaceutical industry experience.

• Ideally, at least ten years of relevant experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

• Strong knowledge and hands-on experience in PKPD, quantitative systems pharmacology and/or physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling.

• Experience developing mechanistic models, or combinations of mechanistic and empirical models, to represent biological or other natural processes.

• Practical experience with pharmacokinetic and modelling software such as Phoenix WinNonlin/NLME, NONMEM or an equivalent platform, and with analytical tools such as R, Python or MATLAB.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence decisions and collaborate across scientific disciplines.

Useful, but not essential: Experience with machine-learning workflows, managing external service providers, or supporting due diligence within physiologically based pharmacokinetic and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modelling.

What you’ll do

• Set the direction for translational PKPD screening and mechanistic modelling across different molecular formats, working with research, non-clinical and clinical stakeholders.

• Design preclinical PKPD/pharmacodynamic studies, interpret the results and communicate conclusions that support project decisions.

• Build mathematical models and run simulations of human PKPD using in-house in vitro and animal data, together with relevant literature.

• Guide project teams on preclinical study design, dose setting for toxicity studies, first-in-human dose selection and clinical trial design.

• Contribute scientific input to regulatory interactions and documents, including Investigational New Drug applications, Investigational Medicinal Product Dossiers and New Drug Applications.

• Advance scientific capabilities in mechanistic modelling and PKPD, solve complex problems and mentor fellow scientists.

Who you’ll work with

You will join one of two closely connected PKPD teams within DMPK and Modelling Sciences. Together, the teams advance the use of quantitative systems pharmacology, physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling and PKPD modelling across the research and development value chain.

Your closest collaborators will include in vivo pharmacologists, in vitro biologists, clinical modelling scientists, toxicologists, clinicians and regulatory affairs specialists. The area is part of Global Research within Research & Development and works with global discovery and development colleagues, project teams and external partners.

About the DTU Metabolomics Core
The DTU Metabolomics Core in the Department of Bioengineering is one of a several Core facilities within the Department that supports a wide range of research and teaching. The area in which the Metabolomics Core specializes is in the chemical analysis of small secondary metabolites from microorganisms, such as bacteria, fungi, and microalgae. This analysis is undertaken in our extensive instrument suite (HPLC, LCMS, GCMS, MALDI etc.), a collection of instrumentation that you will work closely with as our new technician.

The primary job areas of responsibility
As Laboratory Technician in the Metabolomics Core, you will play a key role in the day-to-day operation of the facility in close collaboration with the Facility Manager. Your responsibilities will include:

• Operating and maintaining our analytical instrumentation, including high-resolution LC-MS systems (sample preparation, calibration, QC runs, routine troubleshooting and preventive maintenance in cooperation with service engineers)
• Running samples for internal researchers and external contract projects, from sample preparation to data acquisition
• Ordering and managing laboratory supplies, consumables, and chemicals, and keeping the lab stocked and organized
• Maintaining lab standards: cleanliness, safety, waste handling, documentation, and quality control routines
• Supporting users of the facility with practical guidance on sample submission and preparation
• Contributing to the ongoing development of workflows and procedures in the facility
• Supporting students
In addition to this is it expected that you will take part in some Department duties, particularly involving laboratory and chemical safety. This will be done in close collaboration with a team of 4 other technicians working within the same section that hosts the Metabolomics Core.

Qualifications
We expect that you:

• Hold a degree as a laboratory technician (laborant) and/or a BSc/MSc in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, chemical engineering, or a related field
• Have hands-on experience with HPLC instrumentation. Experience with high-resolution MS (e.g., QTOF) is a strong advantage
• Are experienced in routine laboratory work, including sample preparation, solvent handling, and general upkeep of analytical labs
• Have knowledge of Good Laboratory Practice, safety regulations, and documentation standards
• Are structured, detail-oriented, and able to plan your own work independently

jobs.occupation: Senior ML Data Engineer
jobs.description:
**About GoWish, Ønskeskyen ☁️

**At GoWish, we’re building the world’s leading wish-list and social shopping platform - a place where you can make a real impact and have fun doing it.

We’re on a mission to reinvent gifting for millions. We win together, driven by curiosity, ownership, and bold ideas that turn into real products. We experiment cross-functionally, push for excellence, and keep things playful as we grow - together.

**Team & Role Overview

**We are looking for a systems-minded Senior ML Data Engineer to own the offline-to-online feature infrastructure that powers our real-time recommendation and search engines at scale. You will be building the low-latency data syncs and feature-serving layers that bridge our analytical warehouses with operational databases, caches, and Feature Stores. This is a role for a performance-driven engineer who excels at pipeline orchestration (Airflow, dbt), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Docker), and database tuning, ensuring our recommendation systems receive reliable data under strict low-latency SLAs. If you thrive on solving complex data synchronization challenges, scaling operational storage for millions of users, and acting as the operational bridge between Data Science and Backend Engineering - you will play a critical role in powering our product's core ML capabilities.

**What You'll Do

**

• Offline-to-Online Feature Pipelines: Build and operate resilient feature pipelines syncing transformed data from analytical warehouses (e.g., BigQuery) into operational storage layers (e.g., AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models at scale.

• Pipeline Orchestration and Transformations: Design, test, and maintain robust Apache Airflow DAGs and modular dbt transformations to automate end-to-end data ingestion and feature generation under strict low-latency SLAs.

• Infrastructure as Code and Reliability: Provision, scale, and automate cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and CI/CD pipelines, implementing automated data quality testing and monitoring across all feature syncs.

• Cross-Functional System Design: Partner directly with Data Scientists and Backend Engineers to define online/offline feature contracts, optimize database schemas for sub-second queries, and eliminate training-serving skew for millions of active users.

**What we’re looking for 🌟

****We Imagine That You Have

**

• 4+ years of experience

• Operational Data Pipelines: Proven experience moving batch features from analytical warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake) into low-latency online stores (AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models.

• Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Deep hands-on experience provisioning, scaling, and managing cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and modern CI/CD automation pipelines.

• Pipeline Orchestration & Transformations: Strong track record building, scheduling, and maintaining workflow orchestrations (e.g., Airflow, Dagster) and modular data transformation frameworks (e.g., dbt).

• Database Performance Tuning: Advanced SQL skills across both OLAP and OLTP systems. Ability to optimize schemas, indexing, partitioning, and queries.

It is further seen as an advantage to have experience with:

• Production Feature Management: Experience managing Feature Stores (e.g., Feast, Tecton) or low-latency key-value stores (e.g., Redis) to serve online ML features with zero training-serving skew.

• Real-Time OLA): Experience with ClickHouse, Pinot, Druid or others for ultra-fast aggregations over live event streams.

• Event Streaming: Hands-on experience with streaming tools like GCP Pub/Sub, Kafka, or Flink for real-time feature updates.

Why GoWish should sit at top of your career wish list 💙

At GoWish, we believe great work comes from people who feel energized, supported, and excited to show up every day. That’s why we’ve built a workplace where celebration, growth, and genuine enjoyment are part of the journey - not perks on the side.

Take your birthday off with Happy Birthday Leave, enjoy 30 days of vacation to fully recharge, and join a team that fills the year with events and playful happenings. We invest in your future with pension and insurance, fuel your days with a weekly lunch scheme, and keep you going with unlimited snacks and sodas - because work should feel good.

At GoWish, you don’t just build great products. You build a great work life.

**Practical information

**We collaborate in a flexible hybrid setup, with most of our magic happening at our bright, modern office in Østerbro - perfectly placed between Nordhavn and Østerport Station. We’re ready for you to join us as soon as you are.

👉 Ready to help shape a platform that already empowers 18+ million users (and counting)? Join us at GoWish - and let’s build the future of data-driven innovation together.

Don’t wait to apply - we review applications continuously and may close the position once the right candidate is found.

jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 3000 employees Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, and Consulting.

About the team

Join our Transfer Pricing team of more than 45 colleagues in Copenhagen and Aarhus. We help international and Danish businesses turn complex tax, finance and operating-model questions into practical solutions. You will build your expertise through real client work, structured learning and close collaboration and help clients navigate tax and transfer pricing challenges.

Job Description

You will work on a wide range of transfer pricing projects across various sectors. Together with your colleagues, you will help clients manage operational transfer pricing matters, audits and compliance, and provide both global and local advice. You can expect a steep learning curve, and  responsibilities that grow with your experience - supported by structured onboarding, regular feedback and close collaboration with experienced colleagues. Alongside your client work, you will have opportunities to attend training in Denmark and at Deloitte University in Paris, strengthening both your technical expertise and client-facing skills.

Ready to take the next step in your career? In this role, you will be involved in:

• Collect and analyse financial and business data for transfer pricing projects across sectors.

• Prepare transfer pricing documentation, benchmarking analyses and intercompany agreements.

• Support audits, international tax requirements and country-by-country reporting.

• Turn your analysis into clear client advice, join client meetings and follow up on agreed actions.

• Contribute ideas to proposals, AI-enabled tools and practical improvements to how we work.

We work in a dynamic, international environment with an informal tone, where quality, collaboration and different perspectives are central to how we create value for clients and for each other.

AI-enabled and digital tools are a natural part of how we work. You will learn to use them responsibly to explore data, support research and benchmarking, improve workflows and strengthen deliverables. No prior AI expertise is required - curiosity, sound judgement and a willingness to learn matter most.

We value the community that extends beyond client work. Our employee association brings people together throughout the year - from social events to shared experiences that cut across teams and business units. We celebrate the wins, big and small, and make a point of recognising individual and shared milestones

The role is full-time, and we are looking for professionals for our offices in both Copenhagen and Aarhus, Denmark.

Qualifications

We are looking for Consultants and Senior Consultants with 0–3 years of relevant experience.

We imagine that you are curious, ambitious and motivated by complex challenges. You take ownership of your responsibilities, collaborate openly with colleagues and clients, and contribute to bringing projects to a successful conclusion.

What you bring to the team:

• A relevant academic background, such as law, economics, finance, accounting or business.

• 0–3 years of relevant experience; internships and student roles are also valuable.

• Analytical, conceptual-thinking and problem-solving skills.

• Curiosity about technology and judgement when using AI-enabled tools.

• Clear communication and an interest in turning complexity into practical advice.

• Good energy and a strong client service instinct

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your CV, grade transcript and application in which you present yourself and elaborate on your motivation for pursuing a career in Transfer Pricing and/or highlight relevant projects or previous experience by 5 November 2026. We regularly call for interviews, so send your application already today.

Please do not hesitate to contact Partner Cecilie Emilie Rendtorff at +45 26 61 53 93 or Aske Haahr Lauridsen at +45 20 41 35 92 if you have any questions about the position.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: PhD position at the Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA)
jobs.description:
The Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA) at The Mads Clausen Institute, University of Southern Denmark, is seeking a talented and highly motivated PhD student to work on the development of new theoretical frameworks for describing light–matter interactions in advanced van der Walls heterostructures probed by polaritons generated through inelastic tunneling. The position is funded by a Villum Young Investigator grant awarded to Assistant Professor P. André D. Gonçalves, who will supervise the PhD research.

The position is available starting 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will develop new theoretical frameworks and computational methods to investigate the fundamental limits of polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling in tunnel junctions based on van der Waals heterostructures composed of atomically thin materials. The project will employ a broad range of analytical, semi-analytical, and numerical techniques to explore electrically driven polaritonic phenomena. A major focus will be on harnessing polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling as a tool to probe and manipulate light–matter interactions at the nanoscale, as well as to characterize the optoelectronic response of complex quantum materials.

We welcome candidates with a strong background in condensed-matter physics and/or quantum nanophotonics who are highly motivated and eager to pursue world-class research in theoretical quantum nano-optoelectronics. Experience with scientific programming is expected, while familiarity with numerical techniques is advantageous but not required. The ideal candidate will be enthusiastic about contributing to cutting-edge research in a dynamic and ambitious young research group, supported by the POLIMA Center and its extensive network of international collaborators.

POLIMA is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) for an initial period of 6 years (2023–2028), with the possibility of a 4-year extension. The center is led by Professor N. Asger Mortensen and currently consists of two Professors, three Assistant Professors, a Lab Manager, a Center Administrator, and approximately 10–15 PhD students, postdocs, and visiting scientists. Several POLIMA researchers have attracted prestigious personal grants, e.g., Villum Investigator, Villum Young Investigator, DFF Sapere Aude, Novo Nordisk’s Foundation RECRUIT and Data Science Investigator – Emerging, and Maria Skłodowska-Curie Fellowships. Read more on POLIMA’s website.

We offer a competitive and highly collaborative research environment with close interaction between experimental and theoretical activities. You will join a thriving community of researchers and benefit from a strong network of international collaborators. Our work environment is supportive, dynamic, and designed to foster creativity and the development of innovative projects.

 

We offer:

• A PhD student position in an ambitious and supportive, international research environment.

• A dedicated supervisor research team to support the academic development of the PhD student.

• Access to state-of-the-art equipment, facilities, and infrastructure.

• A competitive salary and social benefits (e.g., health coverage, parental leave, social security, etc.) (https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/international-staff/getting-settled)

POLIMA is located at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense – 1h15min by train from Copenhagen Airport. The University of Southern Denmark offers dedicated assistance and support with various practical, social, and legal aspects (housing, visa, administration, tax, etc.), especially for international candidates through our international staff office (ISO) and the administrative staff at POLIMA.

 

For further information and details about the position, application, and the research center, please contact Assistant Professor Paulo André Dias Gonçalves (padgo@mci.sdu.dk).

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

• 
Motivated application. 

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Master’s and bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (copy of original and an official English translation).  

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

• 
An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish). 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is 31 December, 2026, at 11:59 PM / 23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process. 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step.

The preferred start date is 1 March 2026 (may be adjusted by mutual agreement) or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.
